transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Hi. Well... I guess I'm here because I just can't seem to keep myself together lately. Ever since my daughter left for basic training, I feel like I come home to a dead house, and it's really getting to me. 

I'm sitting there crying in my truck before my shifts start. And at work—I do sheet metal work—I'm missing steps on welding jobs I’ve done for years. I keep snapping at the younger guys on the crew, too. I don't even do the things I normally enjoy anymore. I’ve stopped going out on the water, and I haven't worked on my sculpture at all because I just... I don’t see the point right now. I just feel like I'm falling apart.
Have you experienced periods like this before in your life—times when you felt depressed, lost interest in things, or struggled to function—or is this something completely new for you?

No, this is... it's completely new. I've always been the one who just puts her head down and gets the job done, you know? I've never had a time where I felt like this... where I couldn't just shake it off and keep going. So, no, I've never felt depressed or lost interest in my life like this before. It's just really throwing me.

When your daughter left for basic training, how long after that did you start experiencing these feelings of falling apart—was it right away, or did it take days or weeks before you noticed the change?

I was managing okay right before she shipped out. It wasn't the exact day she left, but... I'd say this all really started within a few weeks of her leaving for basic training. That's when I noticed I was just starting to lose my grip on things.

Since these feelings started a few weeks after your daughter left, have they been pretty constant—like they're there most days—or have there been times when you felt a bit better, even if just for a day or two?

Well, it's pretty much every day. I mean, I guess there might be a day here or there where I'm just too busy at work to think about it for a few hours, but... no, it's pretty constant. I wake up feeling heavy, and it just stays with me. I haven't really had any days where I felt like myself again.
From the time you first noticed these feelings starting, roughly how many weeks or months has it been now?
Well, it's been about a month since she left. And, yeah, I've been struggling like this basically that whole time.

Since this started about a month ago, have you had any periods—even just a few hours or part of a day—where your mood lifted noticeably, or has the heaviness and sadness been pretty much unbroken the whole time?
No, it hasn't really lifted at all. It's just... heavy, all the time. I haven't had any breaks from it.
When you snap at the younger guys on your crew, is that something that's new since your daughter left—something you wouldn't normally do—or have you always had a bit of a temper at work?

No, that's definitely new. I'm usually pretty level-headed on the job. But since she left for basic training, I just... I can't keep myself together. I come home to this dead house, and it's messing with everything. I'm sitting in my truck crying before my shifts even start. And then I get inside and I'm missing steps on welding jobs I've done for years, which is when I end up snapping at the younger guys. It's just... I'm not myself. I've even stopped going out on the water or working on my metal sculptures. I just don't see the point right now.

Since your daughter left for basic training and you started feeling this way, have you had any periods where your mood went the opposite direction—where you felt unusually energized, more talkative than normal, or needed less sleep than usual?
No, nothing like that. I haven't had any extra energy at all. Honestly, it's just been the sadness and feeling drained the whole time. I definitely haven't felt energized or talkative.
